summary: Rabbi Tawil examines the narrative of David and Bathsheba in Shemuel Bet chapters 11 and 12, focusing on how the Hakhamim analyze David's actions. He explores various Talmudic perspectives, including the discussion in Masekhet Shabbat 56A, which attempts to reconcile David's status as the gold standard of kingship with the events described in the text. The class highlights the tension between the literal reading of the story and the interpretive approaches used to understand the culpability of David.
questions: How can David be considered the gold standard of kingship if he committed such a grave sin?
What does it mean when the Talmud says David wanted to sin but did not actually do it?
Why did soldiers in David's army give their wives divorce papers before going to war?
Was David technically guilty of adultery according to the Talmudic analysis?
